title: Bismarck and Fargo: doubling trumpet and piano
summary: He moves from Bismarck to a Fargo job with a woman pianist, ends up playing trumpet with one hand and piano with the other; a Charlie Moffett aside.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Shortly after that, his gig run out, we stayed at a hotel until this gig ran out, then we went from there to Bismarck and played someplace over there. It was cold... Oh boy, it was colder than the world's biggest fanny, boy, I'll tell you.
When that job run out... There was a piano player there in Bismarck, so she sounded me and the bass player and the drummer if we'd go to Fargo with her, because she had a job

in Fargo. And I had to work, and I said, "Well, shit, yeah, the hell with Herb Whitfield. If he ain't got no job, I won't stay here with him. Let him get a job, and then he can come talk to me." So we went to Fargo. And they liked the group, but they didn't like the piano player -- and it was her gig, you know. So they fired her, and then they come back and hire each one individually. Which was all right, because at least we kept the money coming in. And me and the bass player... I had to double on trumpet and piano, one hand with the piano and one on trumpet, you know. You can imagine how that sounded then; I was a horrible trumpet player at that stage anyway, you know. I didn't know what I was doing.
Well, you couldn't have been horrible. You'd been playing with all these bands. You must have had some kind of...
Yeah, but I wasn't talkin' about nothin'. I mean, I had heard Roy, and I know that I wasn't talkin' about nothin', you know. So I said, "Well, shit, I've got to make a living," so...
One hand on the piano and one hand on the trumpet.
One hand on the piano and the other on the trumpet. That's the way I had to do that.
The last guy I saw do that was Charlie Moffett, the
drummer who used to play with Ornette Coleman. He played the drums with one hand and the trumpet with the other!
I don't think I heard him.
That was a long time ago, before he had his family... Anyway, to get back to... So here you were up in Fargo, doing this.
